 font-size: 10pt;">Variable Interest Entities</span></p></td></tr></tbody></table><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">ASC 810 requires the assessment of whether an entity is a variable interest entity ("VIE") and, if so, if we are the primary beneficiary at the inception of the entity or at a reconsideration event. We are required to consolidate a VIE if we determine that we have a controlling financial interest in the VIE. Controlling financial interests will have both of the following characteristics: (a) the power to direct the activities of a VIE that most significantly impact the VIE's</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">economic performance and (b) the obligation to absorb losses of the VIE that could potentially be significant to the VIE or the right to receive benefits from the VIE that could potentially be significant to the VIE. Our variable interest in VIEs</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">are in the form of joint ventures and land and lot option purchase contracts. </span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">We examine specific criteria and use our judgment when determining if we are the primary beneficiary of a VIE and have a controlling financial interest. The significant factors we consider in determining whether we are the primary beneficiary include risk and reward sharing, experience and financial condition of other partner(s), voting rights, involvement in day-to-day capital and operating decisions, representation on a VIE's</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">executive committee, existence of unilateral kick-out rights or voting rights, level of economic disproportionality between us and the other partner(s) and contracts to purchase property from the VIEs.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">We also enter into land and lot option purchase contracts to procure land or lots for the construction of homes. Under these contracts, the Company will fund a stated deposit in consideration for the right, but not the obligation, to purchase land or lots at a future point in time with predetermined terms. Under the terms of the option purchase contracts, many of the option deposits are not refundable at the Company's discretion. Under the requirements of ASC 810, certain option purchase contracts may result in the creation of a VIE that owns the land parcel under option.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:13.2pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-right:5.3pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; These instruments involve, to varying degrees, elements of credit and interest rate risk. Credit risk is managed by entering into MBS forward commitments, option contracts with investment banks, federally regulated bank affiliates and loan sales transactions with permanent investors meeting the segment&#8217;s credit standards. Our risk, in the event of default by the purchaser, is the difference between the contract price and fair value of the MBS forward commitments and option contracts. MANAGEMENT'S DISCUSSION AND ANALYSIS OF FINANCIAL CONDITION AND RESULTS OF OPERATIONS</span></a></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span></span><span style="font-size:10pt">Hovnanian Enterprises, Inc. (&#8220;HEI&#8221;) conducts all of its homebuilding and financial services operations through its subsidiaries (references herein to the &#8220;Company,&#8221; &#8220;we,&#8221; &#8220;us&#8221; or &#8220;our&#8221; refer to HEI and its consolidated subsidiaries and should be understood to reflect the consolidated business of HEI&#8217;s subsidiaries).</span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:10pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold">Key Performance Indicators</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:10pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">The following key performance indicators are commonly used in the homebuilding industry and by management as a means to better understand our operating performance and trends affecting our business and compare our performance with the performance of other homebuilders. We believe these key performance indicators also provide useful information to investors in analyzing our performance:</span></p><table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse"><tbody><tr><td style="width:45.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="width:18.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#9679; </span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">Net contracts </span><span>is a volume indicator which represents the number of new contracts executed during the period for the purchase of homes, less cancellations of contracts in the same period. The dollar value of net contracts represents the dollars associated with net contracts executed in the period. These values are an indicator of potential future revenues;</span></p></td></tr><tr><td style="width:45.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="width:18.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic;">&#160;</span></p></td></tr></tbody></table><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt"><span style="display:none;">&#160;</span></p><table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse"><tbody><tr><td style="width:45.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="width:18.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#9679; </span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">Contract backlog</span><span> is a volume indicator which represents the number of homes that are under contract but not yet delivered as of the stated date. The dollar value of contract backlog represents the dollar amount of the homes in contract backlog. These values are an indicator of potential future revenues;</span></p></td></tr><tr><td style="width:45.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="width:18.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic;">&#160;</span></p></td></tr></tbody></table><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt"><span style="display:none;">&#160;</span></p><table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse"><tbody><tr><td style="width:45.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="width:18.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#9679; </span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">Active selling communities</span><span> is a volume indicator which represents the number of communities which are open for sale with ten or more home sites available as of the end of a period. We identify communities based on product type; therefore, at times there are multiple communities at one land site. These values are an indicator of potential revenues;</span></p></td></tr><tr><td style="width:45.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="width:18.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic;">&#160;</span></p></td></tr></tbody></table><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt"><span style="display:none;">&#160;</span></p><table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse"><tbody><tr><td style="width:45.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="width:18.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#9679; </span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">Net contracts per active selling community</span><span> is used to indicate the pace at which homes are being sold (put into contract) in active selling communities and is calculated by dividing the number of net contracts in a period by the number of active selling communities in the same period. Sales pace is an indicator of market strength and demand; and</span></p></td></tr><tr><td style="width:45.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="width:18.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic;">&#160;</span></p></td></tr></tbody></table><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt"><span style="display:none;">&#160;</span></p><table cellspacing="0" cellpadding="0" style="width:100%; border-collapse:collapse"><tbody><tr><td style="width:45.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#160;</span></p></td><td style="width:18.5pt; vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span>&#9679; </span></p></td><td style="vertical-align:top"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-style:italic">Contract cancellation rates</span><span> is a volume indicator which represents the number of sales contracts cancelled in the period divided by the number of gross sales contracts executed during the period. Contract cancellation rates as a percentage of backlog is calculated by dividing the number of cancelled contracts in the period by the contract backlog at the beginning of the period. Cancellation rates as compared to prior periods can be an indicator of market strength or weakness.</span></p></td></tr></tbody></table><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45.35pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">On January 1, 2026, we acquired a controlling interest in a previously unconsolidated joint venture in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia ("KSA"), that operates and markets itself under the trade name HOV Global. Beginning in the first quarter of fiscal 2026, the results from KSA are included in our consolidated financial statements.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">Consistent with our historical presentation, we will continue to exclude the results of our KSA operations from these key performance indicators generally (unless otherwise indicated) because such operations are not expected to have a material impact on our financial results for fiscal 2026.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">Where we have excluded the KSA operations, we refer to such metrics as being for our &#8220;domestic&#8221; operations.</span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:10pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold">Overview</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-style:italic">Market Conditions and Operating Results </span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45.35pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">The demand for new and existing homes is dependent on a variety of demographic and economic factors, including job and wage growth, household formation, consumer confidence, mortgage financing, interest rates, inflation and overall housing affordability.</span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45.35pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">During fiscal </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'9d3-bc9-c85-ac6-75c2'; -aw-sdt-title:'Previous_Year_P1'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">2025</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt"> and continuing through the</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">first half</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">of fiscal </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'6c0-c97-388-a26-e5a5'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Year_P1'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">2026</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt">, mortgage rates have fluctuated but still remain at a persistently high level. As a result, affordability generally remains challenging for homebuyers.</span><span style="font-size:10pt; font-weight:bold"> </span><span style="font-size:10pt">We have stayed aggressive in our pricing, incentives and concessions in order to align with the current market.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><div style="-aw-sdt-tag:'PG_ec26641f01590406'"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-align:center; font-size:10pt"><span style="font-family: 'Times New Roman';  font-size: 10pt;">30</span></p><div><hr style="width: 100%; color: #000000; background-color: #000000; margin: 1rem 0;"/></div></div></div><div class="Section_31"><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><a href="#TOC_TableofContent" style="text-decoration:none"><span style="font-size:10pt; text-decoration:underline; color:#0000ff">Table of Contents</span></a></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:0pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt;">&#160;</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:10pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">We continue to use our increased inventory of quick move-in homes ("QMI homes") to help meet buyers&#8217; needs for more affordable housing in the existing uncertain interest rate environment. The time between contract signing and closing is shorter with a QMI home as compared to a to be built home, which provides customers with more certainty on their mortgage pricing. The availability of QMI homes also allows us to offer mortgage interest rate buydown assistance, which is a tool we offer through our wholly-owned mortgage banking subsidiary ("K. Hovnanian Mortgage"), to help ease the impact of higher monthly payments from rising interest rates. We pay the cost of interest rate buydowns for customers that qualify through K. Hovnanian Mortgage and decide to use the program. The level of interest rate based incentives utilized differs across our markets and is one of several available options we use to drive sales and close homes.</span></p><p style="margin-top:0pt; margin-bottom:10pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Our emphasis on driving sales pace versus price resulted in domestic net</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">contracts increasing by 1.0% in the</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'999-bf3-06a-83a-aefe'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Year_P3'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">2026</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt"> compared to the prior year </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'b69-b06-3c0-484-2408'; -aw-sdt-title:'Quarter_P5'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">second quarter</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt"> and 2.0% for the six months ended April 30, 2026 compared to the same period of the prior year.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">Within the six-month period, net contracts fluctuated from month to month, reflecting ongoing shifts in market conditions</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">and consumer sentiment, including increased hesitancy from buyers, which we believe was partially attributed to the Iran war.</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">Even with the volatility in the broader economy and affordability constraints, we were able to raise</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">prices or decrease incentives in approximately 44% of our domestic communities during the </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'c37-03d-559-844-982d'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Year_P4'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">2026</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt">.</span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">While the long-term fundamentals of the new home market remain favorable, there remains a great degree of uncertainty due to inflation, tariffs, the continued possibility of an economic recession, employment risk, geopolitical events and the potential for further mortgage rate increases. In particular, the magnitude and volatility of land charges for the Company, and for other homebuilders, have been significant and, as such, have made comparable financial analysis of our industry more difficult. The difference between net income and cash flow from operating activities is primarily caused by changes in inventory levels together with changes in receivables, prepaid expenses and other assets, mortgage loans held for sale, accrued interest, deferred income taxes, accounts payable and other liabilities, and noncash charges relating to depreciation, stock compensation and impairments. When we are expanding our operations, inventory levels, prepaid expenses and other assets increase, causing cash flow from operating activities to decrease. Certain liabilities also increase as operations expand and partially offset the negative effect on cash flow from operations caused by the increase in inventory, prepaid expenses and other assets. Similarly, as our mortgage operations expand, net income from these operations increases, but for cash flow purposes, net income is partially offset by the net change in mortgage assets and liabilities. The opposite is true as our investment in new land purchases and development of new communities decrease, causing us to generate positive cash flow from operations. </span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; Substantially all homes under construction or completed and included in inventory at </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'41e-80d-bbb-20d-03aa'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Period_P107'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">April 30, 2026</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt"> are expected to be delivered during the next six to nine months. </span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:0pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Consolidated inventory not owned, which consists of options related to land banking and model financing, increased $36.2</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">million from </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'922-f8d-ae4-7e9-68a9'; -aw-sdt-title:'Previous_Year_End_P32'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">October 31, 2025</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt"> to </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'e70-200-64f-6ae-c8ad'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Period_P108'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">April 30, 2026</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt">. The increase was primarily due to an increase in land banking transactions, partially offset by a decrease in the sale and leaseback of certain model homes during the period. We have land banking arrangements, whereby we sell land parcels to land bankers and they provide us with an option to purchase finished lots on a predetermined schedule. Because of our options to repurchase these parcels, these transactions are considered a financing rather than a sale. Our Condensed Consolidated Balance Sheet, at </span><span style="-aw-sdt-tag:'e02-71b-136-bc5-8fb8'; -aw-sdt-title:'Current_Period_P109'"><span style="font-size:10pt; font-family: 'Times New Roman'">April 30, 2026</span></span><span style="font-size:10pt">, included inventory of $296.1</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">million recorded to &#8220;Consolidated inventory not owned,&#8221; with a corresponding amount of $180.2</span><span style="font-size:10pt">&#160;</span><span style="font-size:10pt">million (net of debt issuance costs) recorded to &#8220;Liabilities from inventory not owned&#8221; for the amount of net cash received from the transactions. In addition, we sell and lease back certain of our model homes with the right to participate in the potential profit when each home is sold to a third-party at the end of the respective lease. As a result of our continued involvement and the ability to repurchase model homes with below market options, these sale and leaseback transactions are considered a financing rather than a sale. Inflation has a long-term effect, because higher costs for land, materials and labor results in increasing sales prices of our homes. Historically, these price increases have been commensurate with the general rate of inflation in our housing markets and have not had a significant adverse effect on the sale of our homes. A significant risk faced by the housing industry generally is that rising house construction costs, including land and interest costs, could substantially outpace increases in the income of potential purchasers and therefore limit our ability to raise home sale prices, which may result in lower gross margins. </span></p><p style="margin-top:10pt; margin-bottom:10pt; text-indent:45pt; line-height:12pt"><span style="font-size:10pt">Inflation has a lesser short-term effect, because we generally negotiate fixed-price contracts with many, but not all, of our subcontractors and material suppliers for the construction of our homes. These prices usually are applicable for a specified number of residential buildings or for a time period of between three to 12 months.
